text: In 2014-11, we converged. Forty-three of us said "broken immigration system," peaking on 2014-11-20; thirty-five of us said "our broken immigration system" the same day. Mark Takano said it first, on 2013-01-03. Thirty-three of us reached for "comprehensive immigration reform," also on 2014-11-20. That date recurs. On it, twenty-three of us said "action on immigration," twenty of us "executive action on immigration," and nineteen of us "fix our broken." Twenty-two of us noted "the senate passed." Apart from the rest, on 2014-11-11 twenty of us said "men and women who." We record that our language pooled on a single day around a single subject, and that the phrasing was shared before it was widespread: the first-sayer preceded the peak by nearly two years. This is what the record from this era shows of us.
